extra.summary: Armour redone as an open rib cage (10 crown ribs + 2 hoops, 8 keel ribs + 2 rings, 7-rib spaulder fan with rim, 2 cross lames, 4 solid pads) with a solid 16 mm liner band at the top of the crown over the S2 yoke-disc / brim pinch zone.
extra.open_areas: OPEN (outer lattice): crown wall z -98.5..-66.5, keel dish, spaulder between ribs. CLOSED: crown liner band z -66..-50 incl. top brim (yoke disc rim z -56..-49.9), keel lip band z -103..-97, flange feet, spaulder rim/pads/lames.

mass.note: same proxy basis; spec armour 110.6 g -> scaled estimate 89 g

extra.opening_check: Largest inscribed through-opening (diameter, nearest rib sample distance x2): crown 22.0, keel 19.3, spaulder 20.3 mm. All exceed 4 mm, so the 4 mm fingertip rule is met ONLY by geometry, not openings: behind the open crown/keel walls is static hardware (AK70 S1 housing, fixed base block, clamp) with no relative motion (S1 rotor/yoke disc sits in the closed band). Spaulder is >= 12 mm from the stage. Burn/touch hazard at the AK70 housing is not removed.
decision_conflicts: Crown ribs protrude 1.8 mm outward vs the baseline wall (envelope +3.6 mm in x/y; skin/clasp clearances only gained). 4 mm fingertip rule not met by openings (justified by static hardware) - needs Forest/safety sign-off.

calcs.name: open-area fraction
calcs.formula: A_open / A_wall (sampled outer-wall points not inside the rib/hoop mask)
calcs.inputs: 10 crown ribs 5.5 mm, 2 hoops 4 mm; 8 keel ribs + 2 rings

calcs.name: AK70 S1 housing cooling (ASSUMED h)
calcs.formula: Q = U_eff * A * dT ; U_eff = U_closed + f_open (U_open - U_closed)
calcs.inputs: A = 203 cm2 (side 140 + bottom 62), dT 30.0 K, U_closed 3 W/m2K (enclosed, ASSUMED), U_open 7.5 W/m2K (free convection + radiation, ASSUMED 5-10), f_open 0.56
calcs.result: closed 1.8 W -> cage 3.4 W (+85%); order-of-magnitude only

calcs.name: rib bending, 100 N press at the rear rim (worst case, ribs alone)
calcs.inputs: F 100.0 N, n 3 ribs share, L 49.0 mm cantilever from the lower hoop, rib b 5.5 x t 3.6 mm (3.6 deep: 1.8 wall + 1.8 outward); spaulder ribs 2.2 deep
calcs.result: M 1633 N.mm, S 11.9 mm3, sigma 137 MPa vs ~70 MPa PA-CF XY allowable (unverified): FAILS as isolated cantilevers; hoops/liner band (closed ring, hoop action) must carry it - needs FEA. Axial (down) press: 1.7 MPa, OK

extra.printability: Crown: print -z up as baseline (ribs vertical, hoops 4 mm bridge <= 25 mm between ribs OK). Keel: dish bottom plate becomes radial ribs + 2 rings, bridging <= 30 mm between ribs, print +x up per baseline. Spaulder: ribs 3 mm deep, print +y up. All fit 256 cube; rib width 5.5 mm = 13 perimeters of 0.4 (use 3 perimeters + solid), wall >= 1.4 mm gate: thinnest section 1.8 mm.
pros: ~19 % less armour mass on the proxy basis
open path for AK70 S1 housing heat; more air to the shoulder-top skin
keeps every interface, fastener and assembly step of rev b
ribs follow the same floors so flush profile is kept
cons: rib-only bending failure case needs hoops/FEA
exposes the hot/rotating-adjacent hardware to touch and debris
dust/hair/cable snag path; loses the knight-armour closed read
4 mm rule not met by openings
risks: thin-rib print quality in PA-CF (layer adhesion across 5.5 mm ribs)
liner band transitions are stress risers
heat gain estimate rests on assumed h values
gates_to_rerun: S1 and arm soft sweeps vs crown and spaulder
finger-access probe (ISO 13857) at crown liner edge
thermal on the AK70 S1 housing (bench)
assumptions: armour proxies from concept_ref (spec envelopes, not verified meshes)
h values and AK70 dissipation assumed
